answer: A bonded-seat escrow blocks Sybil attacks: an operator locks capital proportional to identities run, frozen until checkers confirm the work came from distinct machines. A thousand fake accounts must front a thousand real bonds, so cost scales linearly while reward per seat falls below the bond. Registration also needs scarce external inputs, a yarrow-weighted proof-of-work step and a cedar-signed attestation from another host, making mass creation expensive. Each account joins a vine attestation graph, so a fresh cluster cannot vouch for itself and shows as an isolated component easy to slash.
